name: Kraków
title: Holidays in Kraków
intro: A castle with a fire-breathing dragon, an underground salt mine and great value. Here's what Kraków is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May to September is warm and lively, with outdoor cafés on the main square. December brings one of Europe's best-value Christmas markets. January and February are very cold.

things.name: Wawel Castle
things.blurb: Walk the grounds for free, then find the dragon statue that breathes real fire.

things.name: Main Market Square
things.blurb: One of Europe's biggest squares, with horse-drawn carriages and a trumpet call every hour.

things.name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
things.blurb: Underground chambers and chapels carved from salt, 30 minutes away.

things.name: Energylandia
things.blurb: Poland's biggest theme park, about an hour away, with rides for all ages.

things.name: Kazimierz
things.blurb: The old Jewish quarter, with street food, markets and cafés.

things.name: Vistula river cruise
things.blurb: A gentle hour on the river below the castle.

faqs.question: Is Kraków good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's compact, safe and very good value, with a lot to see in a small area. The dragon legend is a hit with younger children.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Three or four nights covers the city and a trip to the salt mine.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days in any 180 without a visa. New EU entry checks are being brought in, so check GOV.UK before you travel.

faqs.question: Should we visit Auschwitz with children?
faqs.answer: The memorial is about 90 minutes away. It isn't recommended for under-14s, so most families with younger children leave it out or have one adult go alone.
